title: When the Landfall Wakes
premise: Lena Marchetti runs a salvage crew on the closed mountain rail lines, keeping her head down and her past buried. When rival engineer Cassius Vane hires them to reopen the drowned Cascade Tunnel before his concession permits expire, Lena agrees for money she desperately needs—unaware the tunnel holds the wreck of a train her own father was blamed for derailing twenty years ago. As the crew digs toward the truth, sabotage, a rising river, and Vane's hidden agenda force Lena to choose between clearing her father's name and getting her found family out alive. In the end, she brings every one of them home, exposes the real saboteur at the permit hearing, and lets the tunnel be sealed forever—with the truth finally written into the record.
about_author: Rosalind Reyes is a former track surveyor who spent a decade mapping abandoned lines across the Pacific Northwest before turning to fiction. She writes adventure novels about people who fix things the world has decided to forget.

chapters.title: Dead Rails
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Her crew reroutes a washed-out spur in freezing rain, establishing their competence, their debts, and their unspoken rule: no jobs above the old Cascade line. Emotional beat: weary pride masking an old wound.

chapters.title: The Man with the Permits
chapters.summary: Cassius Vane appears at the crew's bunkhouse with a contract, cash advance, and a deadline: reopen the Cascade Tunnel in six weeks or lose his concession. Lena refuses; her foreman Odell quietly reveals they can't make payroll without it. Beat: dread dressed as opportunity.

chapters.title: Sworn Off
chapters.summary: Flashback woven through present-day packing: young Lena watching her father arrested for the derailment that sealed the tunnel, and the crew's oath never to touch it. She signs anyway, telling herself it's just steel and water. Beat: guilt as a loaded tool.

chapters.title: Up the Gorge
chapters.summary: The convoy fights the switchback road; a bridge collapses under the supply truck, nearly killing new hire Teo. Lena improvises a winch recovery, earning the crew's trust but burning two days. Beat: first blood price of the job.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Teo's POV. At the tunnel's north portal, floodwater stands black behind the bulkhead. Teo finds a rusted lantern that isn't twenty years old—it's five. Someone has been inside recently. Beat: creeping wrongness.

chapters.title: Vane's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Lena confronts Vane about the fresh lantern; he deflects with schedules and penalties, but she notices his survey maps mark a spot far from any plausible collapse. Beat: suspicion sharpening into certainty.

chapters.title: Pumping the Dark
chapters.summary: Odell's POV. The crew battles to lower the water level; Odell, a former miner, recognizes deliberate demolition cuts in the bulkhead—not flood damage. He tells only Lena. Beat: loyalty tested by knowledge.

chapters.title: Halfway House
chapters.summary: A resupply run brings mail and a newspaper clipping someone slipped into the crate: the original derailment inquest, with a witness name circled. Lena realizes someone outside the crew knows why she's really here. Beat: hunted feeling.

chapters.title: The Witness
chapters.summary: Lena hikes out to find the circled witness, Ada Kowalczyk, now a recluse. Ada confesses she saw the brake lines cut—and was paid to stay silent by the railroad's insurer. Beat: grief and fury braided together.

chapters.title: Cut Lines
chapters.summary: Returning at night, Lena finds the generator sabotaged and Teo injured in the resulting darkness. The crew wants out; Lena, torn, offers anyone free passage down. No one leaves. Beat: found family choosing each other.

chapters.title: Inside
chapters.summary: With water low enough, Lena leads the first entry team through the portal. Headlamps find the wreck exactly where it shouldn't be—moved, arranged, tampered with after the fact. Beat: awe curdling into violation.

chapters.title: The Second Map
chapters.summary: In the wreck's mail car, Lena recovers her father's own field notebook, proving he flagged the faulty brakes days before the crash. Vane arrives unexpectedly, demanding they push deeper toward a specific car. Beat: the trap half-visible.

chapters.title: Bargaining with Ghosts
chapters.summary: Lena forces a confrontation: Vane admits the concession's true prize is bearer bonds rumored lost in the wreck, and that he hired her because her name opens doors his can't. Beat: betrayal, but also a strange honesty.

chapters.title: Storm Line
chapters.summary: A spring storm swells the river; the south portal begins to fail. Vane's hired hands try to seize the notebook during evacuation prep, and a fight in the flooding adit leaves one of Vane's men dead by his own greed. Beat: chaos as revelation.

chapters.title: Sealed Choices
chapters.summary: Odell's POV. With both portals compromised, the crew must shore the north bulkhead or lose everything—including the evidence. They work through the night, Odell narrating what family means when blood isn't the tie. Beat: sacrifice freely given.

chapters.title: Ada Comes Up the Mountain
chapters.summary: Ada arrives unannounced with her original sworn statement and a lawyer's letter, having decided twenty years of silence cost more than testimony ever could. Beat: courage arriving late but arriving.

chapters.title: The Permit Hearing
chapters.summary: Back in town, at Vane's emergency hearing to extend his concession, Lena plays her hand: the notebook, Ada's statement, photographs of the staged wreck. The room turns; the bonds claim dissolves; Vane's backers abandon him. Beat: justice outside the law, delivered inside one.

chapters.title: What Vane Carries
chapters.summary: Vane's POV, briefly. Ruined, he meets Lena on the platform and admits his brother died in the derailment—that his whole scheme was a warped search for the same truth. Lena gives him the notebook's duplicate pages. Beat: mercy as the harder victory.

chapters.title: Closing the Portal
chapters.summary: The state orders the tunnel permanently sealed. The crew performs the demolition themselves, placing the charges where Lena's father once stood. Beat: burial as release, not erasure.

chapters.title: Payroll and Promises
chapters.summary: Salvage fees and a historical-society grant clear the crew's debts. Teo is offered a city job and declines; Odell signs on for another season. Beat: warmth earned, futures chosen.

chapters.title: The Record
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. At the county archive, her father's record is formally amended; she files her own report of the expedition, omitting nothing. Walking out, she passes Vane waiting to do the same. Beat: quiet reckoning.

chapters.title: When the Landfall Wakes
chapters.summary: Spring runoff opens the high country. The crew boards a northbound freight to a new line, Lena at the throttle, the mountains forgiving nothing and forgetting less—but carrying them forward all the same. Beat: hard-won peace in motion.
